passages.text: Pseudosasa japonica, the arrow bamboo (Japanese: metake), is a species of bamboo in the grass family Poaceae native to Japan and Korea, but planted worldwide as a horticultural plant.

Description 
This vigorous bamboo forms thickets up to {{convert|6|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall with shiny leaves up to {{convert|25 |cm|in|abbr=on}} long. The culms are typically yellow-brown and it has palm-like leaves. The common name "arrow bamboo" results from the Japanese samurai using its hard and stiff canes for their arrows. It grows up to {{cvt|4|cm}} a day.{{cn|date=November 2022}}

Cultivation
This cold hardy bamboo species (tolerant to 0 °F/−17.7 °C) grows well both in shade and full sun. Pseudosasa japonica does very well in containers and salty air near the ocean. Because it tends to be more shade tolerant than other bamboo species it is often used by gardeners as an understory to a tree-lined living fence. In cultivation in the UK this species has gained the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit.
